title: Switchable day-trader timeframe mode (ch. 39) -- fully configurable, global setting
description:
Ch. 39, 'Choosing Timeframes--the Factor of Five': Triple Screen doesn't hard-code weekly/daily/intraday -- it's built around whatever three timeframes the trader picks, each related to its neighbor by roughly a factor of five. This app currently hard-codes the swing/position-trader pairing (weekly/daily/intraday). Day-trading is the book's other explicit example (25-min/5-min/2-min, or a 39-min/8-min pairing). This is a genuinely large feature -- a new intraday data dependency (needs IBKR live, unlike everything else in this app which works via always-on yfinance), and a real architecture change everywhere the app currently assumes 'weekly'/'daily' as fixed concepts (schema field names, cache table interval columns, calendar-week truncation logic) rather than a generic long-term/intermediate/short-term triple. Product decisions (2026-09-24, by the user directly, see `decisions` below): build it; ship a fully user-configurable timeframe triple (not one of the book's fixed examples); make it a single global app-wide setting, not a per-request parameter.

**Scope split (2026-09-24, this task's own PR, see `decisions` below):** this task's own PR lands only the foundational model (checklist item 2, `app.signals.timeframe`) and the global settings persistence (checklist item 3, `app.trading_mode` + `TradingModeSettingORM` + `GET`/`PUT /api/settings/trading-mode`) -- a real, working, tested piece of the larger feature, not just docs/interfaces. Checklist items 4-9 below are the *original* full-feature breakdown, kept here for historical/traceability context (each is annotated with which dependent follow-up task now actually tracks it) -- they are no longer this task's own remaining scope. See docs/architecture/Backend.md §10 for what's landed vs. still outstanding as of this PR.

checklist.step: Answer the questions below and move this task to 'planned' before any implementation work starts.

Design the generic timeframe-triple model that replaces the app's current hard-coded weekly/daily/intraday assumption: a long-term/intermediate/short-term triple of intervals, validated to roughly follow ch. 39's factor-of-five spacing (decide and record how strictly to enforce this -- a hard validation error vs. a soft warning vs. no enforcement at all, since ch. 39 itself frames the exact ratio as a guideline, not a hard rule). This needs to reach every place the app currently assumes 'weekly'/'daily' as fixed concepts: schema field names (app/api/schemas.py), the OHLCV cache table's interval column (app/data/cache.py), calendar-week truncation logic, and the signal engine's tide/wave/ripple evaluation (app/signals/engine.py). DONE this PR: `app.signals.timeframe`'s `TimeframeUnit`/`TimeframeInterval`/`TimeframeTriple` -- a foundational domain model only; it does not yet touch app/api/schemas.py's existing 'daily'/'weekly' Interval literal, app/data/cache.py's interval column, or app/signals/engine.py's truncation logic (all deliberately deferred -- see this task's own `decisions` entry and the child tasks below).

Add a global app-wide setting (persisted, not per-request) storing the active trading mode (swing/position-trader vs. day-trader) and, when day-trader mode is active, the user-configured timeframe triple. Design the storage (a new settings table/row vs. extending an existing one) and the API surface to read/write it. DONE this PR: `TradingModeSettingORM` (singleton row, same convention as `AccountORM`), `app.trading_mode.get_trading_mode_setting`/`set_trading_mode_setting`, and `GET`/`PUT /api/settings/trading-mode` (`app.api.routers.settings`).

Wire IBKR live intraday data fetching for the short-term (and, if the configured triple's intermediate timeframe is also intraday, that one too) leg of the day-trader triple. Must degrade gracefully to a clear disabled/unavailable state (not an error) when IBKR isn't connected or FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED is false, consistent with every other IBKR-dependent feature's contract in this app (see backend-market-scanner/backend-market-breadth-indicators for the established pattern). NOW TRACKED IN: backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday.

Adapt the signal engine's Triple Screen evaluation (tide/wave/ripple) to operate generically over whichever three timeframes are currently configured, instead of hard-coded weekly/daily/intraday -- this is the core methodology change; needs an elder-signal-reviewer pass given ch. 39's own framing of what changes and what stays invariant when timeframes shift (the Impulse System, confidence scoring, and 6% Rule risk logic should all remain timeframe-agnostic in principle -- confirm this holds, don't assume it). NOW TRACKED IN: backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine (includes the elder-signal-reviewer pass, folding in the former checklist item 9 below).

Update API schemas/endpoints to expose the active mode and the generically-computed signals, decide whether existing weekly/daily-named response fields need renaming or can stay as aliases for whichever timeframe currently fills that role, and regenerate backend/openapi.json + frontend/src/api/types.ts. NOW TRACKED IN: backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api.
Frontend: add a settings UI to view/switch the global trading mode and configure the day-trader timeframe triple. NOW TRACKED IN: frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings.

Unit/integration tests for the generic timeframe evaluation (including a mocked IBKR intraday provider -- no test may make a live network call), the settings persistence/API, and frontend tests for the settings UI. The settings-persistence/API half is DONE this PR (tests/unit/signals/test_timeframe.py, tests/unit/test_trading_mode.py, tests/integration/test_trading_mode.py, all at 100% line/branch coverage); the generic-evaluation and frontend halves are NOW TRACKED IN backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine and frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings respectively.

elder-signal-reviewer pass before merge (this changes core signal/methodology logic, not just plumbing). NOW TRACKED IN: backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine (folded into that task's own checklist -- this PR makes no signal/methodology change, only adds an inert foundational model + settings persistence nothing yet reads).

decisions.rationale: The user was asked directly whether to build this given its scope (a real architecture change, not a UI toggle) and its hard IBKR-live dependency (unlike every other feature in this app). Chose to build it.

decisions.decision: Ship a fully user-configurable timeframe triple, not one of the book's fixed example triples (25-min/5-min/2-min or 39-min/8-min).
decisions.rationale: The user was asked to choose between the book's two fixed examples or a fully configurable triple. Chose configurable, matching ch. 39's own framing that timeframe choice is inherently personal to the trader, despite the higher implementation cost relative to a fixed pairing.

decisions.decision: Day-trader mode is a single global app-wide setting, not a per-analysis-request parameter.
decisions.rationale: The user was asked whether the whole app should switch mode at once (global) or whether a ticker could be viewed in either mode independently (per-request). Chose global -- a much smaller, less breaking API contract change than threading a mode parameter through every signal/analysis endpoint.

decisions.decision: Split this feature into this task's own PR (foundational timeframe model + global settings persistence, checklist items 2-3 only) plus four dependent follow-up tasks: backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday (item 4), backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine (items 5+9, the core methodology change plus its required elder-signal-reviewer pass), backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api (item 6), and frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings (item 7). Each depends_on this task's id (and, where a later one genuinely needs an earlier one's output, on that sibling too -- signal-engine depends on ibkr-intraday since there's no way to meaningfully test generic evaluation against day-trader data without real intraday fetching; api depends on signal-engine; the frontend task depends only on the api task, not directly on signal-engine, since it only needs the settings/other-endpoints' contract, not the engine internals).
decisions.rationale: The task's own description explicitly authorized this split given the genuine scope (a new IBKR-live data dependency plus a real architecture change touching the schema/cache/engine layers) -- landing all 8 remaining checklist items in one PR would make it unreviewable as a single unit and mixes a low-risk, fully-additive foundational piece (nothing existing reads the new model/table yet, so swing mode -- this app's only production mode today -- is provably unaffected) with a high-risk methodology change (genericizing Screen 1/2/3) that needs its own dedicated elder-signal-reviewer scrutiny per CLAUDE.md's own testing/review conventions. Rejected keeping it as one PR: the resulting diff would span data-provider wiring, core signal-engine logic, API-contract renaming decisions, and frontend UI all at once, with no way to land (and get real review coverage on) the low-risk foundational piece independently of the much riskier methodology change. Rejected a 3-task split combining 'API + frontend UI' into one task (as an earlier draft of this decision considered): this codebase's own established convention consistently splits a backend-* API task from its frontend-* consuming task (e.g. backend-trade-journal-entry-notes / frontend-trade-journal-entry-notes, backend-trade-journal-followup-review / frontend-trade-journal-followup-review) since each is governed by a different skill (add-api-endpoint vs. add-frontend-feature) and can be picked up/reviewed independently -- collapsing them into one task would depart from that precedent for no real benefit.

decisions.decision: TimeframeInterval is represented as a (unit, count) pair -- unit one of MINUTE/DAY/WEEK -- with a canonical short string code ('25m'/'1d'/'1w') as the API/persistence encoding, rather than collapsing everything to a single arbitrary minute count.
decisions.rationale: A pure minute-count model (e.g. storing '10080' for a week) was considered and rejected: this app's weekly bars are formed by resampling daily bars into calendar-anchored Saturday-through-Friday bins keyed on Friday (app.data.stooq_provider.StooqProvider._resample_weekly, app.signals.engine._weekly_through_bar_date), a qualitatively different concept from 'N minutes' that a future generic Screen-1/Tide implementation (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine) will still need -- collapsing WEEK into a minute count now would lose that distinction and force it to be reconstructed later. The chosen (unit, count) + short-code model keeps DAY/WEEK's calendar semantics intact while still letting `approx_trading_minutes` compare across units on one common scale for the factor-of-five guideline check. The short string code (not a nested JSON object) is the actual persisted/API shape, matching this codebase's existing 'closed string-enum-like column, Python-layer validation only' convention (OHLCVCacheORM.interval, ClosedTradeORM.exit_reason).

decisions.decision: TimeframeTriple's long_term > intermediate > short_term ordering is a hard validation error (raises ValueError); the ch. 39 factor-of-five spacing guideline itself is only a non-blocking warning (factor_of_five_warnings()), never rejected, using a 2x-10x tolerance band.
decisions.rationale: Ch. 39 itself explicitly frames 'roughly a factor of five' as a guideline, not a hard rule -- and even the book's own canonical 25-min/5-min/2-min day-trading example isn't a clean 5x on both legs (25/5 = 5x, but 5/2 = only 2.5x), which is direct evidence against enforcing any tight band as a hard rule. An inverted or degenerate ordering (long_term shorter than short_term, or two equal legs), by contrast, isn't 'an unconventional but valid trader choice' -- it breaks the Triple Screen premise outright (a 'long-term trend filter' shorter than its own entry-trigger timeframe is simply mislabeled), so that gets hard-rejected instead. The 2x-10x band (not, say, 3x-8x, an earlier draft of this decision that failed against the book's own 25/5/2 example during test-writing) was chosen specifically to admit every one of ch. 39's own worked examples (weekly/daily and 25-min/5-min are both exactly 5x, 39-min/8-min is ~4.9x, and 5-min/2-min is 2.5x) while still catching a triple that's clearly not following the guideline at all (e.g. two legs only ~1.1x apart).

decisions.decision: A previously-configured day-trader TimeframeTriple is preserved (not cleared) in TradingModeSettingORM when the user switches back to 'swing' mode; PUT /api/settings/trading-mode with mode='swing' and no triple in the request body leaves any existing persisted triple untouched.
decisions.rationale: A user who toggles between swing and day-trader mode (e.g. trading swing-style most of the day, day-trading during a specific session) shouldn't have to re-enter their timeframe triple every single time they switch back to day-trader mode. The alternative (clearing it on every switch to swing) was rejected as needless friction with no corresponding benefit -- an unused persisted triple costs nothing while 'swing' is active, since nothing reads it in that state.

decisions.decision: This app's existing swing-mode Tide/Wave/Trigger scheme (weekly/daily/daily-as-Trigger-approximation) is deliberately NOT represented as a constructible TimeframeTriple instance -- DEFAULT_SWING_TRIPLE_CODES is kept as a plain tuple of interval codes ('1w', '1d', '1d'), which would raise ValueError if fed through TimeframeTriple's own constructor (intermediate and short_term are identically '1d').
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md itself documents Screen 3 (Trigger) as a same-day-or-shorter approximation on daily bars ('For a daily-bar app (no intraday feed required), approximate with: today's close crosses back above yesterday's high') -- there is no literal third, faster timeframe in this app's current swing-mode implementation, so its intermediate and short-term legs are the same interval in practice. Forcing this through TimeframeTriple's strict ordering rule would either require weakening that rule (undermining the real invariant it protects for genuinely generic triples) or fabricating a fictitious short-term interval that doesn't correspond to anything the swing-mode engine actually does. Keeping it as a separate, explicitly-non-generic constant -- documented as this scheme's closest analogue, not a real instance of the model -- was judged clearer than either alternative. This constant is not read by any code yet (a documentation/parity placeholder only); backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine is where swing mode's actual behavior gets reconciled with the generic model for real.

decisions.decision: Fixed both blocking review findings on PR #309 (update_trading_mode now ignores body.day_trader_timeframe_triple entirely -- doesn't even parse it -- when body.mode != 'day_trader', instead of only conditioning persistence on it after parsing; and the PUT /api/settings/trading-mode 422 responses entry now declares an explicit content.application/json.schema anyOf: [HTTPValidationError, ErrorDetail], matching GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history's own dual-422-shape convention it already claimed to follow). Also fixed all 4 non-blocking findings in the same pass (stale 3x-8x wording in app/signals/timeframe.py's factor_of_five_warnings() message, app/api/schemas.py's TimeframeTripleOut.factor_of_five_warnings field description, and a test comment; the settings.py module docstring's nonexistent follow-up task id, split into the two real ids; docs/architecture/Backend.md's section renumbered from '## 11.' to '## 10.' -- and its own cross-references in docs/architecture/API.md and this task's/its sibling tasks' `references` arrays updated to the new anchor; and two new boundary-ratio tests (exactly 2.0x and 10.0x) added to TestFactorOfFiveWarnings) -- see backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-followups.json's checklist for those items, now marked done there too.
decisions.rationale: All 6 were filed on this task's own review.comments (2 blocking) or the -followups task's checklist (4 non-blocking) from the same PR #309 review pass; fixing the non-blocking 4 alongside the 2 blocking ones was cheap (small, low-risk, same area of the codebase already open for the blocking fix) and avoids a second round-trip through the followups task for work already in front of the same reviewer. Chose to condition triple-parsing itself on `body.mode == 'day_trader'` (not just gate persistence after parsing) so a malformed day_trader_timeframe_triple supplied alongside mode='swing' can never even raise a spurious 422 -- consistent with the field's own documented 'ignored (may be omitted) when mode is swing' contract, which reads as unconditional, not merely 'ignored for persistence but still validated'.

decisions.decision: The reviewer-requested regression test's final step ('a subsequent switch back to day_trader with no explicit triple restores A') was implemented as a GET confirming A is still persisted, followed by a PUT to day_trader that re-supplies A explicitly -- not a literal PUT with mode='day_trader' and no day_trader_timeframe_triple in the body.
decisions.rationale: TradingModeIn's own model_validator (_require_triple_for_day_trader_mode, pre-existing, unchanged by this fix) unconditionally rejects any PUT with mode='day_trader' and no day_trader_timeframe_triple with a 422, regardless of whether a triple was previously persisted -- confirmed directly against TradingModeIn(mode='day_trader') before writing the test. A literal 'switch back with no explicit triple' request would therefore 422, not 200-and-restore, making the literal scenario as worded impossible to exercise without also weakening that pre-existing, intentionally-required-every-time validation rule -- which is out of scope for this fix (the blocking finding was specifically about the swing-mode overwrite, not about relaxing when a triple must be supplied). The GET-then-resupply sequence still verifies the actual property that matters (A, not B, is what's in storage to build the next day_trader request from) without touching that unrelated validation rule.

questions.question: Should day-trader timeframe mode be built at all, given its scope (a real architecture change, not just a UI toggle) and its hard dependency on IBKR being live (unlike every other feature in this app, which works with no IBKR setup)?
questions.context: This is a product/scope call, not something a worker can decide and record on its own -- it commits the app to maintaining a second, materially different data pipeline and a generic long/intermediate/short-term timeframe model throughout the signal engine and API schema. ANSWERED (2026-09-24T15:13:24Z, by the user directly): yes, build it -- see the decisions entry above.

questions.question: If built, which timeframe triple should ship first -- the book's 25-min/5-min/2-min example, its 39-min/8-min pairing (chosen because 39 minutes divides the 390-minute US trading day into a clean 10 bars), or a fully user-configurable triple?
questions.context: Each has different implementation cost: a fixed triple is far simpler than a configurable one, but ch.39 itself frames the timeframe choice as inherently personal to the trader. ANSWERED (2026-09-24T15:13:24Z, by the user directly): fully user-configurable -- see the decisions entry above.

questions.question: Should this be a global app-wide setting (the whole app switches mode) or a per-analysis-request parameter (a ticker can be viewed in either mode)?
questions.context: This changes the shape of the API contract change significantly -- a global setting is a much smaller, less breaking change than a per-request parameter threaded through every signal/analysis endpoint. ANSWERED (2026-09-24T15:13:24Z, by the user directly): global app-wide setting -- see the decisions entry above.

comments.summary: Blocking: PUT /api/settings/trading-mode doesn't ignore day_trader_timeframe_triple when mode='swing' -- update_trading_mode parses and persists any supplied triple regardless of mode, contradicting TradingModeIn.day_trader_timeframe_triple's own documented 'ignored ... when mode is swing' contract and silently overwriting a previously-preserved day-trader triple. Reproduced directly against a live TestClient: PUT day_trader with triple A, then PUT swing with triple B, then GET -- the stored triple becomes B, not preserved A. No test exercises mode='swing' + a supplied triple.

Blocking: PUT /api/settings/trading-mode's 422 responses entry declares only a description string, with no content/schema -- unlike the 'dual-422-shape convention' it explicitly claims to follow (GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history, which declares an explicit content.application/json.schema with anyOf: [HTTPValidationError, ErrorDetail]). Confirmed in the regenerated backend/openapi.json: this 422 has no content key at all, so frontend/src/api/types.ts generates content?: never for it. Violates CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard ('every documented error case declared in responses={...} ... using the ErrorDetail schema').

Non-blocking: factor_of_five_warnings()'s returned message text, TimeframeTripleOut's OpenAPI field description, and a test comment all still say the guideline band is '3-8x'/'3x-8x', but the actually-implemented band (_FACTOR_OF_FIVE_MIN_RATIO/_MAX_RATIO) is 2x-10x -- stale wording left over from the earlier 3x-8x draft the task's own decisions entry says was widened.

Non-blocking: app/api/routers/settings.py's module docstring references a follow-up task id 'backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-intraday-signal-engine' that doesn't exist; the actual split created two separate tasks (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday and backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine).
Non-blocking: docs/architecture/Backend.md's new section is numbered '## 11.' immediately after the existing '## 9.', skipping 10.
Non-blocking: TestFactorOfFiveWarnings has no test pinning the factor-of-five band's exact boundary ratios (2.0x / 10.0x) -- only interior and clearly-exterior ratios are covered.

review.notes: Independently re-ran: pytest --cov=app (1287 passed, 100% line/branch coverage), ruff check + mypy (clean), yarn tsc -b --noEmit + yarn eslint (clean), alembic upgrade head / downgrade -1 against a throwaway DB (clean), scripts/export_openapi.py + yarn generate:api-types re-run and diffed byte-for-byte against committed backend/openapi.json + frontend/src/api/types.ts (no diff), scripts/validate_tasks.py (no violations). No UI surface in this PR (settings UI deferred to frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings) -- browser walkthrough and e2e suite both explicitly skipped. TimeframeTriple model, migration, and the 4-way task split are all sound; the two blocking findings are the swing-mode triple-overwrite bug and the missing 422 content schema on PUT /api/settings/trading-mode above (the latter surfaced by a background code-review pass dispatched during this review and confirmed independently before being added here).
